The hunter, the hunter, whose worship uses his mouth as a sacred vessel, the hunter, whose eye is like a flower, whose eye is the flower, where the Lord whose foot is joined to his, the Kalathi mountain, the Kalathi mountain, the Kalathi mountain. If you ask about the mountain where Shiva resides, who, like a cloud, killed a mad elephant that rushed down from the mountain’s side, causing Uma to fear, and flayed its skin, as the waves of many waterfalls and springs flow, and the ancient wisdom shines like a jewel, scattering pearls like rays of light, the Kalathi mountain. Many waterfalls with waves, many springs with eyes, as the ancient wisdom shines, scattering luminous pearls like rays of light, the Kalathi mountain.

If you ask about the mountain where Shiva resides, who, seeing the penance performed by Bhagirathan who purified the earth, granted grace and accepted the turbulent Ganga into his matted locks. It is Kalathi mountain, where fragrant karagil wood burns brightly, emitting a delightful scent. If you ask about the mountain where Shiva resides, who, to subdue Salandhara, who could not be countered by any means, created a method to pierce him, it is Kalathi mountain, where golden light shines like melted gold, dispelling darkness, as trees adorned with precious jewels yield their treasures and embrace them. Kalathi mountain, Kalathi mountain, Kalathi mountain. If you ask about the mountain where Shiva resides, who crushed the fiery-haired Ravana with his toe. If you ask about the mountain where Shiva resides, who pressed down the great mountain with his finger, it is Kalathi mountain, where the striped-bow-hunting men, as they traverse the long mountains, cause fear among elephants, tigers, and lions.

Kalathi mountain, Kalathi mountain. If you ask about the mountain where Shiva resides, who is known to both Brahma and Vishnu, who sought his feet and crown, it is Kalathi mountain, where Venkai trees adorned with golden flowers bloom, as young women and men, with minds full of love, wander. Standing here, listening to the conversations. If you ask about the mountain where Shiva resides, who remained unyielding to those of many doctrines and even to those who were ungrateful, it is Kalathi mountain, where thick groves on the hill abound, where monkeys play with their young, standing amidst fragrant sandalwood trees. Those who are skilled in singing with Tamil verses about Kalathi mountain, where Shiva dances in the burning ground, will easily attain the celestial world, the celestial world, the celestial world.

We shall continue our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 787, Vambara Varivandra Sarukkam, Thirugnanasambandha Nayanar Puranam, as bestowed by Deivasekkizhar Peruman. Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman proceeds towards Thirukalathi mountain, singing that pathigam. He reaches the bank of the Ponmugali River in front of Thirukalathi mountain. With a large gathering of devotees surrounding him and praising him, they all come forward to welcome him. Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman bows down to the bank of the Ponmugali River.

As the devotees press closer from all sides, Pillaiyar, the one who possesses grace, proceeds to the foot of Thirukalathi mountain, where the Lord, who is like a medicine on the mountain, resides, and bows down to the ground. Deivasekkizhar Peruman composes the verse: After singing the refined, melodious composition, praising the devotion of Thiru Kannappar, the multitude of great ascetics came, praised, and crossed the Ponmugali river. While the great ascetics pressed on all sides, Pillaiyar, the grace-bearer, who is the medicine sought by Brahma and Vishnu, came and bowed down at the foot of Thirukalathi mountain, which revealed itself. Deivasekkizhar Peruman composes the verse: “The Lord, who is like a medicine on the mountain, Thirukalathiyappar, resides there. It is true that the best medicinal herbs are found on mountains. Among these medicines, it is very rare to find the best ones without searching.

“But here, the Lord is a rare medicine. That rare medicine, which cures the incurable disease of birth, the Lord, resides very clearly and brightly on Thirukalathi mountain, very simply.” The verse describes Pillaiyar, who, accompanied by a great throng of devotees who praised and worshipped, reached the bank of the Ponmugali River and bowed. As the virtuous ascetics surrounded him on all sides, Pillaiyar, the child-saint, bowed at the foot of Thirukalathi mountain, where the Lord, the elusive medicine sought by Brahma and Vishnu, revealed Himself. In many places in the Thevaram, the three great saints have praised the Lord as a medicine. The verses of Thevaram speak of Him as medicine, saying, “He is the medicine, and if one needs medicine, He is it, and He is the mantra, tantra, and medicine.” Here, Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman calls the one who is like medicine, medicine. If He is said to be outside, it means the outer space of pure consciousness.

“Along with this, there is also a reference to the sacred story of Thiru Kannappa Devanayanar.

“The Lord Himself resides on the mountain as medicine. Thiru Kannappa Devanayanar sees blood flowing from one of the Lord’s eyes. The meaning of this is that he searched for medicine on that mountain to cure the wound in the Lord’s eye, who is medicine, and then brought and applied that medicine after finding it.

“Furthermore, the historical reference is subtly hidden here: Thiru Kannappa Devanayanar, possessing his own eye as an effective medicine readily available, yet unaware of it, searched for many medicines on the mountain.

“Later, realizing that his own eye was the medicine for the wound in the Lord’s eye, he gouged out his eye and applied it to the Lord as medicine.

“Thus, Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman worshipped the Ponmugali River, crossed it, and reached the foot of Thirukalathi mountain. There, with overflowing love, he prostrated himself, falling to the ground with all eight limbs touching the earth. Having bowed and risen, he continued to worship the sacred mountain, ascending the great stone steps. “He ascended the great stone steps, worshipping the mountain, and entered the flourishing golden temple through the jewel-studded gateway where throngs of celestials gathered. After circumambulating the temple, he stood before the Lord, offering praises with folded hands above his head, and then prostrated himself. It was as if he saw the fruit of his worship when he beheld the revered hunter-saint, and he fell at his feet.” Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman, who bowed in reverence at the foot of the mountain, ascended the great stone steps of Thirukalathi mountain while continuing his worship.

“Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman, who bowed down at the foot of the mountain, ascended the great stone steps of Thirukalathi mountain while continuing his worship. Generally, Saivites refer to Mount Kailash as Thirumalai (sacred mountain).

“Here, too, Thirukalathi mountain is referred to as Thirumalai. It is said by enlightened souls that this is the Southern Kailash on earth, equal to the Northern Kailash. That is why Nakkirar Deva Nayanar composed the ‘Kailai Paathi Kalathi Paathi Anthathi.’ Thus, Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman ascended the great steps of such a sacred Thirumalai, Kalathi mountain. Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman ascends, continuously worshipping. He is said to ascend while worshipping, meaning he ascends while contemplating the Lord on that mountain. The story of Karaikkal Ammaiyar walking on her head up Mount Kailash comes to mind here.

“Pillaiyar, showing this tradition to the world and guiding it, ascends the mountain while contemplating and worshipping the Lord. These steps are none other than the steps ascended by Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar. We saw in the puranam of Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar that these are the great steps of principles.

“Accordingly, these steps, which are principles, lead to the Lord who resides on the mountain, the Lord who transcends principles.

“Thus, Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman reaches the golden temple of the Lord. Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman reaches the Lord’s sacred mountain. At the entrance to the sacred mountain, all the celestials stand guard. It is a truth found in the Puranas like Kanda Puranam that these Devas, seeking their positions and heavenly enjoyments, performed meritorious sacrifices, and when difficulties arose while experiencing those positions, they reached Kailash, waited for many days at the Lord’s front gate, and were relieved of all their troubles. These Devas cannot enter without Nandi Peruman’s permission and stand outside.

“However, true devotees always have the right to enter to worship and serve.

“Therefore, they enter and worship the Lord. Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman performs worship before that glorious golden temple, that sacred mansion. He goes before it and performs the worship of bowing and rising before the Lord.

“After that, Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman worships the sacred feet of Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar, who eternally resides there. The worship of bowing and rising before the Lord is completed by worshipping Kannappa Deva Nayanar. This indicates that the worship of the Lord is incomplete without the worship of His devotees. Pillaiyar illustrates this truth.

“Therefore, Deivasekkizhar Peruman states here, “It was as if he saw the fruit of his worship when he beheld the revered hunter-saint, and he fell at his feet.” This implies that the fruit of worshipping the Lord is fulfilled by seeing and worshipping Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar. Just as one finds the meaning in books. Just as one finds the benefit in religious texts, attaining the Lord, who is the supreme reward obtained from religious texts, is explained by Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman here as worshipping Kannappa Deva Nayanar. The four paths of Chariyai, Kiriyai, Yogam, and Gnanam illuminate the means to attain liberation and reach the Lord. Attaining the Lord through these Chariyai, Kiriyai, Yogam, and Gnanam is possible. These Chariyai, Kiriyai, Yogam, and Gnanam serve as spiritual practices.

“The Lord attained through these practices is present, but attaining the Lord not only serves as a means but also as a means to worship devotees.

“Therefore, worshipping devotees itself is explained here as the ultimate benefit and the complete practice. Worshipping the Lord is the means to unite with devotees. The truth that worshipping the Lord unites one with great devotees is realized here. The sacred words of Thirukkovaiyar state, “He gave me to serve the lineage of great devotees.” This is like stating a benefit for a benefit, a profit for a profit. Seeing the Lord is understood here as experiencing the Lord. These are all very rare ideas and thoughts.

“Now, the next verse: The genuine form of love that arises in the heart, and within that love, the untainted Lord with matted red hair and a red eye on His forehead, as if seeing both together, the surging desire flows like water rushing down a slope. Pillaiyar, who partook of the nectar of wisdom from the golden bowl given by the daughter of the golden mountain, joyfully rises and bows many times. In the temple where Thiru Kannappa Devanayar resides, his form, which forgot himself and clearly saw nothing but the Lord, was indeed the embodiment of love, wasn’t it? We contemplated in the puranam of Kannappa Devanayar that he shed the former attachments of accumulated births and became the form of incomparable love, under the shadow of abundant light. His love for the Lord’s feet overflowed and became his very form. Thiru Kannappa Devanayar’s boundless penance in his previous life manifested this blissful love.

“Therefore, seeing Thiru Kannappa Devanayar, who embodied love, and the unsullied Lord, who resided within that love, together in one place, his fervent desire increased even more. Seeing both of them together in one place, that desire surged even more, and like water rushing down a slope, Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman joyfully rose and bowed many times. He was the one who had partaken of the nectar of complete wisdom from the golden bowl presented with grace by the creeper-like Umaiyammai, the daughter of the king of the green golden mountain.

“Therefore, the place where the Lord resides steadfastly is love itself. The Lord, with His grace, swiftly takes the form desired by those who contemplate Him in the lotus of their hearts with love. As Thiru Navukkarasu Peruman’s sacred words state, “In the hearts of those who think of Him, His form and grace will appear.” Therefore, the Lord will reside most brightly where there is love. In other places, He will reside for some time as long as the thought of love exists.

“But here, where Thiru Kannappa Devanayar, who embodies the surging love, resides, Here, where Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar, who embodies the surging love, resides, the Lord eternally resides with great brilliance. Love is not a visible object; it is a concept.

“Therefore, we cannot see love directly; it is not perceptible to the eye. However, that abstract love reveals the inner love through emotional expressions like tears. The Thirukkural states, “Is there a latch to restrain love? The tears of the loving reveal it.” Therefore, we cannot see love with our eyes, but here, that love is vividly manifested as a clear form, perceptible to the eye, in the form of Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar on Thirukalathi mountain.

“The Lord Shiva, the unblemished one, who resides within that love, which is not an object of perception for the eye, That embodiment of love, the pure Lord Shiva, is clearly manifest, becoming an even more brilliant form of grace, perceptible to the eye there on Thirukalathi mountain.

“Therefore, when he saw the embodiment of love, Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar, and the Lord, who is the embodiment of grace, at the same place and time, he rose. When he saw Thiru Kannappa Deva Nayanar, he saw the form of love that captures the Lord, and the Lord who resides within that love.

“Thus, he saw both. At that moment, Gnanasambandha Peruman’s desire and love increased. His devotion surged even more. He worshipped there, and seeing the fruit of that worship, he prostrated himself and rose again. His prostration, not yet complete, he prostrated and rose again. Just as water flows rapidly from a higher ground to a lower ground, that desire spread rapidly in Pillaiyar’s sacred heart, and he joyfully rose and bowed many times.

“Even after completing the prostrations according to the rules, from three to eleven namaskarams (bows) in Ashtanga (eight limbs), Panchanga (five limbs), or Thrayanga (three limbs), he bowed countless times beyond measure. The reason for this was the overflowing love. As he worshipped there, Deivasekkizhar Peruman composes the next verse, stating: “With tears flowing from his lotus-like eyes, he sang a melodious pathigam, filled with immense joy and love that held him back, praising the Lord’s feet. With great difficulty, he left the temple, and upon reaching the foot of the sacred mountain of the Lord, whom Brahma and Vishnu could not reach, he bowed down. The king of Puhali, Thiru Gnanasambandha Peruman, then entered the great matham (monastery) shown by the devoted followers and happily resided there.” Deivasekkizhar Peruman composes the next verse: With tears flowing from his lotus-like eyes, he stood and sang a melodious pathigam, the immense joy and love residing within him holding him back, praising the Lord’s feet.

“He could not leave that place, yet with great difficulty, he departed, came to the foot of the Thirukalathi mountain, the Lord of whom Brahma and Vishnu could not reach. There, the great devotees showed him the matham, and the king of Puhali, Pillaiyar, entered and resided there happily.

“At this time, the Thirukalathi mountain pathigam composed by Pillaiyar is not available to us due to our lack of merit. Our reflection now resumes.

“The Thiruppathigam composed by Pillaiyar at this time, the Kalathi Malai Thiruppathigam, is not available to us due to our lack of merit.

“Let us go on reflecting.” Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Peruman Adiyarkku Nallaruliya Periyapuranam, Part 788. Vambaravarivandu Sarukkam. The Legend of Tirugnanasambandhar Nayanar. The Lord, whom even the greatest find it hard to know, the ruler of the seven worlds, the master of countless celestial beings, seated on the hill of Tirukkalaatti, that sweet nectar. In the city of Shambha, surrounded by fragrant groves where flowers bloom, he dwelled, delighting in worshiping His feet with flowers brought by buzzing bees, singing and enjoying in the holy city.

At that time, as Tamil customs did not prevail in the regions to the north and west, he, like the celestials who sing devotional songs daily to the moon-crested Lord, with his consort, went and worshiped Kailaya in the north, and Tirukketaaram, a sacred place with a pond of lotus flowers, singing devotional songs in pure Tamil. He sang of Kokaranam, where the Lord crushed Yama; he sang of the glory of Tirupparuppadam. He sang of Indran’s blue mountain. He sang praises of the Lord’s word-garland and other offerings. He sang of the devotees adorned with holy ash, surrounded by the Great Father, and continued to delight in that sacred place.

Thus, Peruman Sekkizhar meticulously composed the hymns of Peruman Tiruppadalkal, just as Lord Tirugnanasambandhar, while staying in Tirukkalaatti, had visited the northern holy sites and sung devotional songs. Peruman Sekkizhar explains this narrative thus: through these hymns, it is understood that the Lord is unknowable to all except those who have attained the state of self-knowledge. To those without knowledge, He is unknowable. After attaining the gaze of wisdom, He stands visible to the wise, giving His grace as their eyes. He possesses all worlds and beings as His own, as if they were fatherless. If He owns all worlds, it means He creates all these worlds, universes, and realms from Maya, sustains them, and reabsorbs them into Maya, being the support of that Maya.

Thus, all inert matter is His possession, and all sentient beings are His servants. To such a Lord, countless hosts of celestial beings come to worship on the mountain of Tirukkalaatti. Lord Tirugnanasambandhar goes to worship the Lord of Shiva, who is seated on the mountain of Tirukkalaatti, as that nectar, at all times. The time for worship in the temple is prescribed by the Agamas, from Tiruppalli Ezhuchi to Tirunardha Jaamam, generally six times a day. In some temples, these timings may be more or less.

Thus, at all prescribed times for worship, he visits and worships the Lord of Tirukkalaatti. North of Tirukkalaatti, the northern boundary of the regions is the Himalayas, and the western boundary of the regions to the west is the western sea. As Tamil customs do not prevail in these regions, Lord Tirugnanasambandhar goes to all those regions. Instead of going to worship, he stays in the sacred place of Tirukkalaatti and beholds and worships all the northern holy sites through yogic vision, composing devotional songs. If so, does Lord Tirugnanasambandhar not visit people living in countries where other languages are spoken? Should the grace of Shiva not spread to those countries?

Is Pillaiyar’s compassion limited only to the extent of Tamil people and Tamil lands? Even if those regions are lands where other languages are spoken, does Pillaiyar not have the duty to uplift the people who speak those languages?

Thus, various questions arise. At this point, Peruman Sekkizhar, at the beginning of Pillaiyar’s legend, describes sixteen aspects of Pillaiyar’s divine incarnation. “Let the purity of Tamil prevail over other languages” is one of those divine incarnation objectives. “The glory of all directions will be conquered by the South” is another divine incarnation objective.

Therefore, Pillaiyar incarnated to make the South conquer the glory of all directions, to make Tamil prevail in all language customs, and to offer His grace to all directions and all languages in a state of preparedness. Just as the Lord has revealed the Vedas, Upanishads, Smritis, Itihasas, Puranas, and Agamas according to the preparedness of beings, similarly, Pillaiyar also grants grace according to the preparedness of the beings and the people living in their respective places. In order to bestow grace upon them, He has revealed the Lord’s divine pronouncements in Tamil. Whosoever speaks any language, regardless of the country they belong to, if they use it properly, their state of preparedness will be elevated.

Therefore, it is to convey that Pillaiyar’s devotional songs are capable of encompassing all beings, all people speaking all languages, transcending the boundaries of language, time, and place, that the Lord has willed this.

Thus, while remaining in the sacred place of Tirukkalaatti, He beholds all the northern holy sites through His yogic vision and composes devotional songs appropriate for each place. Pillaiyar usually goes to each holy site and sings. This is Pillaiyar’s practice.

But now, only through yogic vision, He worships and sings in those places. It is stated in the Agamas that through yogic vision, one can attain the state of directly perceiving and knowing everything, transcending the limitations of time and space of others, while being in one place. We can see this through the devotional songs that Pillaiyar has composed for the northern holy sites.

Thus, while remaining on the mountain of Tirukkalaatti, He worships Kailaya and composes devotional songs. Tirukkalaatti, the Southern Kailaya, is a place where humans and celestials worship together.

However, in the Northern Kailaya, only celestials directly go and worship the Lord. This Tirukailaya is believed to be the Prakrita Kailaya, the earthly Kailaya, located on the slopes of the Himalayas.

The formless Kailayam, pervading everywhere, which is the abode of Lord Shiva, is different. It transcends these thirty-six principles from Prakriti to Nada and shines as the sky of wisdom through knowledge. That Kailaya mountain exists for the sages to behold after transcending all these principles.

The bamboo grows tall. O Lord of Kalahasti, your divine feet are worshipped. May the destruction be easy and salvation be attained. The black. Those who desire them will ascend to heaven. With fragrant hills and great pearls.

The waves of the sea, the divine Kalahasti, the pearls, the full flowers. All are praised on the shore. The great waves. Seven great ones are praised.

The Lord of Kalahasti. May the earth and the various trees be destroyed. The shore. The beautiful garland of the Lord. Vishnu. Without the river, the shore.

May you worship the divine feet and be liberated. The sound of the lyre is heard from the sky. Even though he left Thirukkalahasti, my Father’s divine feet remain in my heart. He praised the Lord and took leave. When the Pillaiyar departed from Seerkazhi, he set out with the intention of worshipping all the places in the Thondai region.

Therefore, while staying at Thirukkalahasti, he decided to worship one of the foremost places in the Thondai region. The desire to worship the Lord of Thiruvotriyur grew stronger, and so he set out towards Thiruvotriyur. Why did the Lord make Thirugnanasambandha Peruman feel the urge to worship Thiruvotriyur? It was for him to depart from Thiruvotriyur, go to Thirumayilai (Mylapore), and perform a divine miracle there.

Therefore, with the divine intention to worship Thiruvotriyur, our Pillaiyar departed from Thirukkalahasti. Accompanied by a multitude of devotees who sang of the earth’s glory, he, who was born to uphold the Vedic path, departed from the mountain of Thirukkalahasti, crossing mountains and forests, and previous abodes. He worshipped many abodes of the Lord. As he came from Thirukkalahasti towards Thiruvotriyur, he visited the places he had previously worshipped and other divine places along the way. These places include Thirukkarai, Thirukkallil, Thirunindravur. This Thirunindravur is the abode of Poosalar Nayanar, and includes Vadathirumullaivayil and other places.

We do not have the Thiruppathigam composed by Thirunindravur. He visited many such places along the northern bank of the Paali river. This Paali river carries along with its waters the jewels, gold, and precious goods. Sandalwood and other fragrant substances float in its waters. The northern bank of this prosperous Paali river. This Paali river is also called Pazhaiya Palaru and Kūvam river.

Visiting many such places, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, the one who attained divine knowledge, reached the place called Thiruvekadu, where the Lord resides. Let us resume our reflection. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. The Periya Puranam, Volume seven hundred and ninety-three, authored by the divine Sekkizhar Peruman, concerning the Vambara Varivandu chapter on the life of Thirugnanasambandha Nayanar. He then came to Thiruvallithayam, worshipped, and praised the Lord who resides there, speaking of his divine form. He then went to Thiruvotriyur, which is by the sea, to worship the Lord. When the devotee, filled with great longing, reached the great city. He was welcomed. This is the three thousand and thirtieth verse. Arriving at Thiruvekadu, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman worshipped the radiant golden temple of the Lord.

He composed a Thiruppathigam there. Thiruvekadu is one of the Thevaram-praised places in the Thondai region. It is located in the Vellore district, near Chennai, near Avadi. The Thiruvekadu Karumariamman temple is currently famous.

However, it is also a place of great glory, being a Thevaram-praised place where Thirugnanasambandha Peruman worshipped the Lord. It is located on the banks of the Paali river, also called Pazhaiya Palaru, and the Kūvam river. The Lord’s name is Vedapureeswarar, Verkattu Nader. The Goddesses’ names are Palambigai, Verkanniammai. The sacred water is Velayudha Theertham.

Here, the Vedas, Murugapperuman, Parasara Muni, Atri, Gujara, Angirasa, Vasishta, Gautama, Kashyapa, Dindi, Mundi, Yagnadatta, Viradagni, and other sages, as well as the Panchapandavas, Sibi Chakravarthy, Vanan, the nine planets, and the Ashtadikpalakas, have worshipped the Lord. It is a place where the Vedas worshipped the Lord.

After the great deluge, the four Vedas, as white Vel trees, worshipped the Lord here. Because the four Vedas, as Vel trees, worshipped the Lord, this place came to be known as Velkadu, Verkadu. It is one of the miraculous places where the Lord granted the divine wedding scene to Agasthiya Muni. Murugapperuman came to this place and created the sacred water, Velayudha Theertham, with his Vel. When Vishnu was playing, having drunk the ocean, he dropped the Sankha Panchajanyam from his hand.

Later, worshipping the Lord at this place, he regained it. It is said that Adiseshan, who was present during Vishnu’s worship, resided here and declared that snakes would not bite those who live here.

Therefore, to this day, no one here suffers from snake bites. Hence, this place is known as Visham Theendapathi (the place untouched by poison). It is also the place where Muruga took avatara, and he has a shrine here. Guru Pooja is performed on the Mulam star in the month of Karthigai. The main deity is Vedapureeswarar. On the wall behind him, the divine wedding scene of Shiva and Parvati is depicted in relief.

Murugapperuman worshipped here to obtain the Lord’s blessings to kill Surapadman. This is the place where Murugapperuman, after imprisoning Brahma, worshipped the Lord here and sought forgiveness.

Here, one can see Murugapperuman in a posture of worshipping the Shivalingam. The forms of Agasthiya Muni and Suta Muni are present in the temple. It is a belief among the people of this region that those who worship the Goddess Palambikai of this place, the Goddess Jagadambikai of Thiruvallithayam, and Goddess Vadivuḍaimmai of Thiruvotriyur on the same day will attain all blessings in this life and the next. The reference to the Lord residing under the white Vel tree is evident from the verses of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman’s Thiruppathigam, ‘Velkadu’. We saw that Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, who came to this place, composed one Thiruppathigam. It is the fifty-seventh Thiruppathigam of the first Thirumurai, set to the tune of Pazhamthakkaraag Pann.

This Thiruppathigam is as follows: Praise the divine feet of the bridegroom of Thiruvekadu, O Goddess. O Deva, who has arisen with immense longing. He who danced with the serpent coiled around him, took form as Verkadu. The celestials sang praises. The bhutas sang. He who turned his back in fear.

The knower of the Vedas, Verkadu. For those who offer incense and flowers, there is no suffering. The Ganga flows.

The Lord with matted locks, Verkadu. Those who worship with a humble heart will be saved. Even if sins are revealed, they will be destroyed. He who defeated Yama, in the city of Veyil, is sung by you. Those who worship with song can overcome all obstacles. O Lord, who wears the crescent moon, the king of Verkadu, who is worshipped with devotion.

He who performs service with determination. He who offers sacrifices on the white skull. He who destroys sins. He who is praised. The great city of Mummathil, which is difficult to conquer. Verkadu, the abode of the wise.

Those who can speak of it can reach it. This is the ultimate goal. The radiant white moon adorns his crown. The king of Verkadu, who is worshipped with devotion. Those who remember to worship him will surely attain greatness. The one who offers sacrifices in the white skull.

He who is praised. The divine gift flows down the scenic slopes of Anekatangavatham.

The Lord resides there. Reaching his divine feet is truth. Ravana, devoid of compassion, rose with pride. His valor extinguished, he became a beast. Adorned with serpents, he became the Lord of Anekatangavatham.

The Lord of Anekatangavatham, who resides with pure grace. Those who do not know the great path. They perish. Fallen, like the disciples of the Buddha. Those who seek danger. O those who know danger, listen.

Anekatangavatham is divine. The ancient era, the flourishing world. Good is the Tamil Gnanasambandhan. Speak the truth, and sorrow will vanish. Otherwise, sorrow will remain. Sorrow will remain.

Sorrow will remain. He who is praised.

The Lord of Anekatangavatham, whose divine feet are adorned with waterfalls.

The Lord with matted locks, wearing the moon, who attained immense greatness. He who is in Anekatangavatham. He who is praised by those of good origin, who crushed the forces of death, whose flags are many. He who wears the serpent. He who is adorned with the mountain. He who lifted the desired offerings.

His strong arms, dark as the sky. He who made him a dancer with his finger. This Aneka. Tangavatham, this holy place. Blissful it is, praised by Vishnu and Brahma. O Lord of Anekatangavatham, who rises in meditation.

Who will be destroyed if they do not follow? O divine ones, who guard the earth. Praising Anekatangavatham, the abode of the virtuous. O Lord of Kaazhi, who embraced the divine. Indran touches the Anekatangavatham, with unending praise. Sing of Gnanasambandhan’s songs, and live.

Sing of Gnanasambandhan’s songs, and live. He subdued the demon’s masculinity, who then transformed into a fish, becoming eternal and inseparable from Vishnu. The hunter, who became a hunter of the forest, spoke with two languages. He who has no tongue, and speaks of seven things, the forest of Venda Mango, the forest of Ver, with two languages. The faithful, worshipping Namban’s feet, sang with Sankara Gnana Sambandhar’s pure Tamil, and attained virtue.

Thus this thiruppathigam concludes. The illustrious Gnana Sambandhar, after reaching and worshipping the shining golden temple situated in Thiruverkadu, sang this thiruppathigam. The great Perumaan, Sekkizhar, states that after worshipping and singing the thiruppathigam, the minds of the enemies were vanquished. He then proceeded to Thiruvalithayam. Thiruvalithayam, the place which Gnana Sambandhar worshipped and sang the thiruppathigam, is currently known as Paadi, near Chennai. It is one of the poetically sung places in the Thondai region, very close to Avadi.

The presiding deity here is known as Valliswarar, Valithayanathar, and the Goddess is Jagadambal, Thayamai. The Bharadwaja Theertham is the sacred pool here. Bharadwaja, Rama, Hanuman, Surya, Chandra, Indra, and Valian, the black bird, amongst others, worshipped here and received boons. Sage Bharadwaja was cursed and born as a black bird named Valian. To be freed from this curse, he came to this place in the form of a black bird, created a sacred pool, worshipped the Lord, and was freed from his curse. A legend also states that Brahma had two daughters, Kamalavalli and another, whom Vinayagar married.

Devaguru Brihaspati’s elder brother’s wife, Menaka, cursed him. To be freed from the sin that afflicted him, on the advice of Sage Markandeya, he performed penance here and received the grace of Lord Shiva. The temple’s vimana is of the beautiful Gajaprushta style. Not only is it a Thiru Murai sthalam, but it also features the ‘Thiru Pugazh’ songs of Arunagirinathar. The Brahmotsavam takes place in the Tamil month of Chithirai. Vikrama Chola worshipped the Lord of this temple and was blessed with progeny, as evidenced by several inscriptions.

One inscription states that, after bringing Sundarar Gnanasambandhar from Thiruvengadu, they performed puja here and settled the local priests in this town. For the sustenance of the priest family performing the puja, land was granted as a subsidy. It is mentioned that the paddy given was in the name of Thiru Gnanasambandhar. It is also known from inscriptions that the emperor, Tribhuvana Chakravarti, Rajaraja, built the Kshetrapala Pillaiyar temple and donated lands for offerings. Vijaya Kanda Gopala Devar brought dancing women from Kanchipuram and settled them here, and also provided ornaments and vessels for the Goddess. Inscriptions also reveal that he gifted ornaments and vessels to the Goddess.

This place can be reached from a short distance from Vellivakkam and Korattur. Thiru Gnana Sambandhar has beautifully sung the natural beauty of this place, saying: ‘Valithayam, where the shade of the blooming groves exudes honey, Valithayam, where the fruits of the areca palms are laden with honey, Valithayam, a garden where bees swarm, emanating fragrance.’ He further proclaimed, ‘Those who consider worshipping Valithayam as their life, are the great ones in this world,’ thereby emphasizing the significance of worshipping this sacred place. Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, who arrived at this glorious temple, sang the thiruppathigam beginning with ‘Patharo’du palarum’ (with devotees and many others). This thiruppathigam, the first in the third pathigam of the first Thiru Murai, is set to the tune of Nattapada. This thiruppathigam was sung and gifted to us by Thiru Soundara Bala Amma of Sivakasi. Hail the feet of Valliswarar, along with Jagadambal. First Thiru Murai. Tune: Nattapada. ‘Palrum poliyam malar angai punal thoo’vi otha solli ulagathavam tham thozhu yethu uyar senni matham vaiththa. Those who remember the feet of Thandavanan, and sing Gnana Sambandhar’s Tamil verses, will ascend to the celestial realms. Those who ascend to the celestial realms.

Hail Thiruvalithayam. Thiru Gnana Sambandhar proceeds to worship at Thiru Otrriyur.

Let us proceed with our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. The great Periya Puranam, authored by Thiru Sekkizhar, volume seven hundred and ninety-four. The Puranam of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, who is embraced by swarms of bees. He then proceeded through the streets, reached the gopuram, and sang ‘Thiruppathigappu’. The thiruppathigam sung for Thiru Otrriyur is set to the tune of Panjamam. Goddess Thiruvadiyudaiyamai, Hail Her feet.

Thiru Gnana Sambandhar Nayanar’s sung Thirukkadaikkappu.

‘Vidaiyavan, worshipped by heaven and earth, the Soma Veda’s singer, adorned with conch shell earrings, residing in Otrriyur. The earth dances ...with blooming eyes and powerful grace. He who possesses unwavering resolve, wears the tiger skin, and accepts alms. He resides in Otrriyur. His divine grace flows like water, the primordial Lord who is the fortress. The bumblebee, the moonflower, the konrai flower, the radiant crescent moon, He resides in Otrriyur.

He resides in Otrriyur. He who has taken refuge in Dharma, who wears the sacred thread, whose chest is adorned with the holy ash. He resides in Otrriyur. Those who have renounced, who are ever-present, whose form is radiant, who are worshipped by the world. He resides in Otrriyur. He who stands with unwavering grace, His feet adorned with anklets and the konrai flower, He who holds the vast konrai flower and somanai leaf, He who stands with Uma, resides in Otrriyur.

The world rejoices in His grace. He who resides in Otrriyur, with His divine grace, is worshipped by all. He who adorns himself with the holy ash from the cremation ground, who was struck by an arrow from the Gana warriors. He resides in Otrriyur. He who is described as a madman, whose body is wrapped in tiger skin, who is surrounded by devotees. He resides in Otrriyur.

Thiru and Maruga, Thirumal, and other deities cannot see Him. They who worship His divine feet, are freed from sin and attain salvation. He resides in Otrriyur. Those who meditate on His divine feet are freed from sin. He resides in Otrriyur. Those who wear peacock feathers and saffron robes, who are knowledgeable in the Vedas, who are free from worldly attachments.

He resides in Otrriyur. He who has sung these ten verses of Tamil, praising and worshipping the Lord of Otrriyur, will attain bliss. He who has attained the eternal wisdom, is indeed the Lord who resides eternally in Otrriyur. This is the essence of these thiruppathigams. The first verse mentions ‘Sadaiyan, Sama Vedan,’ indicating the Lord’s great fondness for the Sama Veda, as sung by Thiru Gnana Sambandhar.

Thus, near the temple ...he performed ‘Thirukkadaikkappu’ and completed the thiruppathigam. Bowing down at the gopuram, he entered the divine gateway of the Lord of Lords. After circumambulating, he prostrated before the pure Lord. Thiru Gnana Sambandhar then sang the 1032nd verse, praising the Lord with matted locks, his heart overflowing with love. Tears flowed from his eyes as he sang. He then went forth and resided in Otrriyur, bestowing eternal wisdom upon the world.

The 1032nd verse speaks of the Lord with matted locks like masses of gold. Thiru Gnana Sambandhar’s heart was filled with immense love for the Lord, who pervades everywhere. Overcome with emotion, tears streamed from his eyes as he sang praises before the Lord. Although Thiru Gnana Sambandhar sang this thiruppathigam, due to our shortcomings, it is not available to us.

Thus ...after singing the thiruppathigam and coming out of the temple with his devotees, he stayed in Otrriyur with great affection. This was because, in Thiru Mayilapuram, the miraculous event concerning Poombavai was about to unfold, and Thiru Gnana Sambandhar was divinely inspired to remain in Otrriyur. ‘Ulavatha Gnanam’ means eternal wisdom. This signifies that Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, by his divine grace, would bring forth eternal wisdom. In the thiruppathigam he would sing in Thiru Mayilapuram, the verse beginning with ‘Maninil piranthar perum payan’ (The great benefit of being born on earth) clearly explains the purpose of life and the establishment of Saivism. The woman who died from snakebite, through Thiru Gnana Sambandhar’s thiruppathigam, attained eternal life and merged with Shiva. This is the essence of the verse where Thiru Sekkizhar describes Thiru Gnana Sambandhar as one who attained eternal wisdom for the world’s salvation.

Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, who attained eternal wisdom, would, through his wisdom and hymns, bring about immortality in Thiru Mayilapuram. In that thiruppathigam, the verse beginning ‘Maninil piranthar perum payan’ signifies the ultimate truth of life and the establishment of Saivism. The woman who died from snakebite, through Thiru Gnana Sambandhar’s hymn, attained eternal life and merged with Shiva. This is alluded to by Thiru Sekkizhar when he says Thiru Gnana Sambandhar attained eternal wisdom for the world’s salvation. Thiru Sekkizhar thus lays the groundwork for the miraculous event that would soon take place in Thiru Mayilapuram. In the following verses, the miraculous story of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar reviving Poombavai in Thiru Mayilapuram will unfold.

Thiru Sekkizhar will narrate this story. Let us go on contemplating. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. The great Periya Puranam, authored by Thiru Sekkizhar, volume seven hundred and ninety-five. The chapter of the swarming bees. The Puranam of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar Nayanar. Thiru Gnana Sambandhar is residing in Thiru Otrriyur.

Meanwhile, in Thirumayilai, also known as Thirumayilapuram, lived an devotee named Sivanesar, a merchant by lineage. Thiru Sekkizhar begins to narrate the story of this devotee, Sivanesar. ‘Pillaiyar lived in such a manner.

Now, let us speak of the noble merchant, the esteemed descendant of Thirumayilapuri, who lived in the city with great fame.’ Thiru Sekkizhar proclaims verse 1033: ‘In such a state, Pillaiyar resided in Thiru Otrriyur. In the ancient and glorious city of Thirumayilapuri, famed for its greatness, lived a noble descendant of a great merchant family.

Let us now recount a historical event that occurred concerning his character.’ Thiru Sekkizhar thus narrates. Sivanesar was a devotee born in the great merchant lineage, specifically from the lineage of great merchants. His greatness lay in his devotion, which became the cause for the historical event that follows. His life story is intertwined with that of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar. Previously, many events unfolded concerning Pillaiyar in various places.

Now, we begin to narrate the story that took place in Thirumayilai, concerning the merchant. Thiru Sekkizhar proclaims verse 1034: ‘He accumulated vast wealth, enjoyed its fruits, and his prosperity knew no bounds.’ Thiru Sekkizhar elaborates in verse 1034 on how this descendant of the merchant family possessed immense wealth. He possessed great wealth, engaging in trade and possessing valuable goods that brought him profit. He imported goods from foreign lands, thereby accumulating wealth. As Thirumayilapuram is a coastal city, he had numerous ships in the harbor. He imported rare goods from foreign countries on his ships, and after obtaining government permission and undergoing inspection, he brought them into the country.

He traded these goods, accumulating vast wealth.

Thus, he was blessed with boundless prosperity. His name is Sivanesar. Thiru Sekkizhar explains this in verse 1035: ‘Having known himself truly, he wholeheartedly dedicated himself to service, with great love, shedding falsehood, and embracing the truth as the real substance.’ Sivanesar is the name of that devotee. He is one who knows himself truly. What does it mean to know oneself truly? According to Saiva Siddhanta, it means realizing that God Shiva is the supreme being, the ultimate controller.

Souls are His servants. These servants attain liberation (Mukti) by serving God and shedding their impurities. It is understood that this human birth, the worlds, and the experiences are granted by God for the purpose of shedding impurities and attaining liberation. It means understanding these truths expounded in the scriptures and, without faltering, living in accordance with them, serving God. Those who live thus are said to know themselves truly, according to Saiva Siddhanta. In short, who are those who truly know themselves?

They are those who know themselves and their Lord, as stated in the Sivagnanabotham’s introductory verse. Thiru Sekkizhar praises the devotee Sivanesar, saying, ‘Having known himself truly, he wholeheartedly dedicated himself to service, with great love, shedding falsehood, and embracing the truth as the real substance.’ He served Sankara, the bestower of happiness. Those who know themselves truly realize that this life is full of suffering.

Therefore, they wish to escape this suffering and attain eternal bliss, the bliss of union with Shiva. Sankara is the one who removes suffering and bestows this eternal bliss.

Thus, they desire to attain Him and serve Him. This is natural for those who know themselves truly. Our devotee Sivanessar also knew himself truly and therefore served Sankara. To serve God, the essential foundation is to have love for God.

Therefore, the devotee Sivanessar, with immense love and devotion, dedicated himself to service. He shed falsehood and embraced the truth as the real substance. Falsehood, as described by Thiruvalluvar in the Thirukkural, refers to delusion, mistaking unreal things for real. It is the deluded perception that mistakes fleeting worldly things for the eternal truth. This perverted knowledge is called delusion, which is falsehood. The devotee Sivanessar has shed this falsehood.

Not only that, but he has also attained enlightenment by realizing that Shiva is the ultimate reality. He understood that this reality is dependent on God’s grace, as stated in the Thirukkural: ‘If one lives dependent, and loses dependence, one perishes.’ He firmly resolved this in his heart.

Therefore, the devotee Sivanessar steadfastly adhered to the righteous path of Saivism he had embraced. His name is Sivanessar, as proclaimed by Thiru Sekkizhar. This name is a meaningful appellation, known as ‘Yogaruudhi’ in Sanskrit. Verse 1036 states: ‘He possesses the characteristic of having matted locks, diligently serves the devotees, with a melting heart devoid of hypocrisy, adheres to a path free from attachment, rejects other faiths, and upholds righteousness.’ Thiru Sekkizhar further elaborates on the virtues of Sivanessar. He is always united with the devotees of Lord Shiva, who has matted locks. His heart melts with sincere devotion.

He is constantly united with devotees, his heart melting with love. His heart is free from hypocrisy, and he longs to be united with devotees. This state of his mind is ceaselessly maintained. His state is such that ...his heart melts with love for devotees. As a chaste wife becomes angry with those who lack love for her husband or who insult him, so too does a chaste wife keep away from those who lack love for her husband and who insult him.

Similarly, devotees who are devoted to Shiva and His devotees hate and reject those who lack love for Shiva. This is the characteristic of their love. ‘Those who lack love for Shiva, lack love for devotees, lack love for any being, lack love for themselves. Why speak to such ignorant beings? They will remain estranged in birth after birth. You should not associate with them.’ This verse from Sivagnana Siddhiyar Thiruviruttam advises, ‘Do not associate with those who lack love for Shiva.’ Such individuals will lack love for any being. This verse warns against associating with them.

The quality of rejecting those who lack love for Shiva and His devotees is a sign of righteousness. The rejection of those who lack love for Shiva and His devotees is considered ‘setram’ (anger or righteousness). It implies removing evil, which is a good deed.

Therefore, Thiru Sekkizhar describes this as ‘seelam’ (virtue or conduct). The love for devotees and the aversion to non-devotees are the characteristics of Sivanessar’s heart. Thiru Sekkizhar thus highlights the elevated spiritual state of Sivanessar. Jainism and Buddhism, which are contrary to Vedic traditions, were prevalent during that time. These faiths, not content with their own limits, sought to destroy other Vedic religions. They posed numerous obstacles to the true Saiva path.

Therefore, it was necessary to curb their proliferation and confine them to their own limits. This was essential for the welfare of the world and for self-preservation. This situation existed not only in the Chola and Pandya kingdoms but also in the Thondai region. This is evident from the context.

Therefore, Sivanessar possessed such righteousness. Unlike him, people today lack spiritual knowledge and devotion. They are indifferent to the decline of religion, showing no concern for their faith. They lack both spiritual knowledge and devotion. The learned Desikanar, in his commentary, urges such people to study this Puranam thoroughly.

Let us resume our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. The great Periya Puranam, authored by Thiru Sekkizhar, volume seven hundred and ninety-six. The chapter of the swarming bees. The Puranam of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar Nayanar. Thiru Sekkizhar recounts the life story of the devotee named Sivanesar. He continues: ‘Having known the truth of the Supreme Being, who wears matted locks, and partaken of His divine grace, the world rejoiced.

He rejected the false teachings of Jainism and Buddhism, thereby glorifying the devotees. Hearing of this, Sivanesar, filled with joy, dedicated himself to the service of the great leader, who possessed immense wealth and whose feet were worshipped by countless beings. Day and night, with unwavering devotion and love, he engaged in serving and listening to the accounts of His grace.’ Thiru Sekkizhar thus composed verses 1037 and 1038. As we saw, the devout Sivanesar, who lived according to the Saiva path, heard from devotees about the divine birth of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar in the Kaunthinya lineage of the priestly class in சீர்காழி, his partaking of divine wisdom, and his ability to refute the erroneous doctrines of Jainism and Buddhism, thereby guiding the world to truth. Sivanesar rejoiced upon hearing this. Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, in his hymns, refuted the doctrines of other faiths, pointing out their flaws in the tenth verse of each thiruppathigam, thereby admonishing those who strayed from the Vedic path and establishing the truth.

He exposed the flaws and shortcomings of the other faiths. These were the tidings that Sivanesar heard during that time. As devotees narrated the glories of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, Sivanesar listened with joy. When devotees gathered, they spoke only of the glories of Lord Shiva and His devotees. Only pretenders engage in vain, perishable talk.

Thus, Sivanesar lived, rejoicing in the news of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar’s advent and his hymns. He dedicated himself to the feet of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, the leader of சீர்காழி, who was filled with divine wisdom and grace. With unparalleled reverence and unwavering love, day and night, he constantly meditated on the grace of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar, praised His divine qualities with his words, and listened to the accounts of His divine deeds from devotees. These became the sole pursuits of his life. Thiru Sekkizhar continues his narrative in verses 1039 and 1040.

At that time, Sivanesar, who was indeed a great financier, surpassing even Kubera in wealth and status, lived prosperously. Thiru Sekkizhar states that Sivanesar possessed wealth far exceeding that of Kubera. This highlights the superiority of Sivanesar’s wealth. What was its specialty? All of Sivanesar’s wealth was dedicated to the worship of devotees and the temple.

However, Kubera’s wealth was not so used.

Therefore, Sivanesar possessed wealth superior to Kubera’s. While he lived a married life, the wealth valued in married life, according to sages, is progeny. Thirukkural states: ‘The auspiciousness of marriage lies in the wife and the blessedness of children.’ Thiruvalluvar emphasizes the importance of children in the chapter on married life. He dedicates the first two chapters of the ‘Ilvaazhkai’ (domestic life) section to ‘Ilvaazhkai’ (domestic life) and ‘Vaazhkai Thunaiyalam’ (the companion in life), and the third chapter to ‘Puthalvarai Peru’thal’ (having children). The first chapter is ‘Ilvaazhkai,’ the second is ‘Vaazhkai Thunaiyalam.’ The tenth verse of the chapter ‘Vaazhkai Thunaiyalam,’ which discusses the virtues of a life companion, concludes by stating the importance of children: ‘The auspiciousness of marriage lies in the wife and the blessedness of children.’ This verse, which concludes the chapter on the greatness of a wife, who is a companion in domestic life, highlights the wealth of children. This verse serves as an introduction to the next chapter, ‘Puthalvarai Peru’thal.’ What do the wise consider true good fortune?

It is the good qualities and deeds of one’s spouse. That is the greatest fortune one can receive. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. The great Periya Puranam, authored by Thiru Sekkizhar, volume seven hundred and ninety-seven. The chapter of the swarming bees. The Puranam of Thiru Gnana Sambandhar Nayanar. Thiru Sekkizhar continues to narrate the story of the devotee Sivanesar. He states in verses 1037 and 1038: ‘From the day he was born, he lived according to the righteous path, devoted to the great one, and partook of His divine grace, thereby elevating the world.
